pattern: Specify-written requirements retain STEP-only authorship (issue #22)
evidence: Issue #22 (https://github.com/pzfreo/specify-core-rust/issues/22) explicitly requires a stable STEP-only marker on Specify-authored PMI and recognition by existing.rs. Rust adds provenance=specify-core:written:v1 only for marked requirements; Python has no such field. The pinned haecceity alpha.8 reader exposes tolerance descriptions and per-item consumed IDs; the other markers require raw Document slots or inverse DESCRIPTION_ATTRIBUTE references to those IDs. tests/pmi_provenance.rs checks default PMI on GRM-02 (using the committed shaft fixture when absent from the corpus, without explicit thread answers), and explicit M2/M3 threads and straight knurl on corpus GRM-03 when available. An exported corpus missing GRM-03 fails. The tests also cover emitted requirement kinds, repeated writes, reserved UDA metadata, two sizes on one aspect without identifier tags, EXPRESS validity and byte preservation of imported NIST AP242 PMI on a shared face. docs/pmi-provenance.md specifies exact fields and matching rules. Frozen Python oracle captures are retained.

path: write.warnings[*knurl on *: the intent states no *]
pattern: a knurl from Python's intent, its turned_knurl parameters filled in from DIN 82
evidence: The maintainer's decision Q4/Q15 (docs/questions.md): a knurl is written as AP242's turned_knurl, which needs at least three of number of teeth, tooth depth, root fillet, helix angle and hand beside the diameters and pitch (WR2; a diamond's helix angle, WR9); Python's intent states pattern, pitch and diameter only, so the Rust writer derives the rest from the knurling standard (src/standards.rs knurl_parameters: teeth round(pi d/P), depth P/2 of DIN 82's 90 degree profile, root fillet the knurling wheel's crest radius, IS 3403:1981 and IS 6776:1980 4.3) and says so in a warning, as decided. The knurl itself is written as Python's line ('straight knurl on turned_steps:0') and reads back in both engines' terms as a knurl note on the same faces; verified by read-back (tests/writer.rs, knurls). Python writes no turned_knurl, only its text route and a UDA.

pattern: a g6 diameter Python's reader garbles, and reads with no deviations
evidence: The intent's nominal is 6 (the pin's Ø6 shaft, g6). Python reads back 3.006: OpenCascade's reader cannot return a tolerance whose deviations are both below nominal and garbles the value (writer.py docstring: 'Ø70 g6 reads back as 35.0145'). haecceity reads the nominal as written. Python reads no upper or lower deviation either; the Rust reader reads the fit's class, compared as the limits the class states (ISO 286 g6: -0.004/-0.012 at 6 mm, the intent's own), which the writer checks the intent's limits against before writing.

pattern: a g6 diameter Python's reader garbles, and reads with no deviations
evidence: The intent's nominal is 70 (the spool's Ø70 g6, turned_steps:89); Python reads back 35.0145, OpenCascade's garbling of a tolerance wholly below nominal, which writer.py's docstring cites with this very number. haecceity reads 70. Python reads no upper or lower deviation either; the Rust reader reads the fit's class, compared as the limits the class states (ISO 286 g6: -0.010/-0.029 at 70 mm, the intent's own), which the writer checks the intent's limits against before writing.

pattern: a p6 lower deviation whose sign Python's round trip loses
evidence: The intent states p6 on the spool's Ø130 (turned_steps:70) with upper 0.068 and lower 0.043, ISO 286's p6 at 130 mm (both above nominal). Python reads back lower -0.043: OpenCascade's plus-minus form cannot hold a range wholly above nominal (writer.py's docstring on fits). The Rust writer writes the class p6, read back and compared as the class's limits +0.068/+0.043.

pattern: a distance -0.05/-0.1 Python's reader garbles
evidence: The intent states distance 10, upper -0.05, lower -0.1 (scenario value '-0.05/-0.1'). Python reads back value 5.05 and no deviations: OpenCascade cannot return a tolerance wholly below nominal (writer.py docstring). haecceity reads 10 with -0.05/-0.1, as written.

pattern: a lower deviation Python reads with the wrong sign
evidence: The intent states +0.1/+0.05 (scenario value '+0.1/+0.05', apply: upper 0.1, lower 0.05). Python reads back lower -0.05: OpenCascade's reader loses the lower deviation's sign (writer.py: 'The writer negates the lower tolerance'). haecceity reads +0.05.

pattern: a datum no tolerance references, read back
evidence: Datum A on the plate's top face is in the intent and written; OpenCascade's reader imports a datum only when a tolerance references it (writer.py docstring), which is why the warning exists. haecceity writes and reads it (tests/writer.rs unreferenced_datums_are_warned).

pattern: Python's three parts of one product are one part here
evidence: Python (XCAF) lists CTC-02 as three parts and refuses the assembly for its PMI; haecceity has one part per product definition (question Q7), so Python's three intents name the one Rust part three times and the writer refuses 'a part is written once'. With Q7 settled the comparison applies; an assembly with PMI from elsewhere is written by add mode (Q6).

pattern: Python's two parts of one product are one part here
evidence: As CTC-02: XCAF's two parts are one product definition in haecceity (question Q7); Python's intents name the one Rust part twice.

pattern: Python's parts of one product are one part here
evidence: Python fails inside its text route ('expected one B-rep representation, found 0'); the Rust engine has one part per product definition (question Q7), so Python's per-XCAF-part intents name the one Rust part more than once ('a part is written once').

pattern: Python's parts of one product are one part here
evidence: As CTC-02 RC: Python fails in its text route; Python's per-XCAF-part intents name the one Rust part more than once (question Q7).

pattern: an intent item on no faces listed, the rest written where Python fails in OpenCascade
evidence: On 25 mfcadpp parts (mfcadpp, mfcadpp_holdout, mfcadpp_regressions) and cgb217 Python's own intent has a hole's size, locations and position with faces [] (e.g. mfcadpp/1004 holes:16; holes whose bores are not cylinders the rules keep). Python's write then fails inside OpenCascade ('StepShape_DimensionalLocation: Null Reference' on the mfcadpp parts, 'expected one B-rep representation, found 0' on cgb217). As question Q17 decides, the Rust writer writes the rest of the intent and lists each such item in not_written with the reason ('the size on holes:16 names no faces, so nothing in the file can carry it (question Q17)'); the file is verified by reading back and passes the EXPRESS check (tests/writer.rs a_hole_on_no_faces_is_listed_and_the_rest_written on mfcadpp/1004, a_pattern_on_no_faces_is_listed_and_the_rest_written on cgb217).

pattern: written where Python fails in its text route
evidence: Python fails appending its text route ('expected one B-rep representation, found 0': its anchor search finds no ADVANCED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION); the intent (material, general tolerance) is written by haecceity and verified by reading back.

pattern: answers stored by Python that Python cannot resume
evidence: Python stores the answers with a fingerprint of the input's faces, then re-exports the geometry through OpenCascade, whose centroids' zero components change sign; its fingerprint of the file it wrote no longer matches (checked: flanged_spool_132, stored f39f4952..., Python's fingerprint of its output c8eb6e8e..., no rounded centroid differs). The Rust writer keeps every geometry byte, so its fingerprint matches and the answers resume.

pattern: a Python-written (schema 1) file does not resume in the Rust engine
evidence: The payload is read (tests/resume.rs pythons_stored_answers_are_read) and its face count matches, but Python's fingerprint hashes OpenCascade's centroids, whose zero components carry other signs than haecceity's (plate: Python [-50.0, -0.0, -0.0], Rust [-50.0, -0.0, 0.0]; equal numbers, tests/resume.rs a_python_fingerprint_differs_only_in_signs_of_zero). The Rust engine cannot verify the faces, so it does not resume (the file is analysed with its PMI as its own). Q14 (decided 2026-10-09) keeps schema 1 read exactly as before, so this is the specified outcome; schema 2, which both engines write, fingerprints zeros unsigned, and the two engines' schema 2 fingerprints of these files are equal (tests/cross_engine.rs schema_two_fingerprints_are_the_same_in_both_engines).

pattern: Python's write fails its verification on items with no faces; Rust writes the rest and lists them (Q17)
evidence: Captured from specify-core with its ISO 286 extension (branch iso286-3150; docs/questions.md Q8, 'Recapture source'), which applies this part's answers where the earlier specify-core refused its Ø558.8 diameter. Python's own intent has the size (H11, 0.11/0.0, clearance for M10) and the position of two hole patterns, hole_patterns.linear:84.85.86.87.88.89 and :78.79.80.81.82.83, with faces []; its write raises VerificationError naming exactly those four ('limits 0.11/0.0 not in file' twice, 'position on [] missing or wrong' twice). As question Q17 decides, the Rust writer writes the rest (material, general tolerance, finish, edges) and lists each of the four in not_written ('the size on hole_patterns.linear:84.85.86.87.88.89 names no faces, so nothing in the file can carry it (question Q17)'; checked by running specify-core write --accept-defaults with the oracle's analysis), verified by reading back; the same file is the cross-engine check's nist/nist_ctc_05_asme1_ap242, which OpenCascade opens and reads (tests/cross_engine.rs).

pattern: Python's parts of one product are one part here
evidence: Captured from specify-core with its ISO 286 extension (branch iso286-3150; docs/questions.md Q8), which applies this file's answers. Python's write then fails inside OpenCascade ('StepShape_DimensionalLocation: Null Reference'; its part 0 intent has two hole patterns' sizes and positions and six locations with faces [], as on the mfcadpp parts); Python's three per-XCAF-part intents name the one Rust part more than once (question Q7: parts 1 and 2 are surface models that are in Rust's part 0), so the Rust writer refuses 'a part is written once' and the CLI 'has no part 1' before writing.

pattern: the report counts the dimensions written under the general tolerance (#63)
evidence: Issue #63 (https://github.com/pzfreo/specify-core-rust/issues/63): the writer writes the dimensions the general tolerance covers (general.rs) with their nominal alone, and counts them in one report line, `N dimension(s) under the general tolerance` (with `part:` in an assembly), rather than listing each. Python writes none of them, so it has no such line. A part with PMI from elsewhere (Mode::Add) gets none and no line. Shared planner, #75: slice-one General rows now also appear in Add mode after stored dimensions enter specified; deferred General rows retain the old omission.

pattern: shared-frame location retains six decimal places in millimetres (#75)
evidence: Shared planner, #75: on holdout/363 the shared geometry nominal on [15] from [23] writes 2.238489 mm at Specify's six decimal places; Python's frozen per-member location is 2.23849 mm. The writer oracle reads the actual STEP value and compares it at its existing strict tolerance. This entry covers only that measured value difference; answered location tolerance and support are unchanged.

evidence: Shared planner, #75: the frozen spool intent states Ø62 +0.03/0 on [55]; quiddity::dimensioning identifies the same bore by its defining faces [34,55]. pattern: shared hole-size support uses complete defining faces (#75)
evidence: Shared planner, #75: the frozen Python intent sizes a subset of the recognised bore faces; quiddity::dimensioning v0.4.0 uses the complete defining support of the same hole or equal-hole group. The writer oracle reads the removed subset and added complete-support roots explicitly. Nominals and answered ISO 286 fit classes are preserved; writer verification checks the class against the answered limits. The oracle comparison can expand class limits only on its old intent face set, so the newly keyed full support reads as a class without numeric limits. Only these exact measured roots are covered; deferred owners remain unchanged.

The writer oracle reads the removed subset and added complete-support roots explicitly. Nominals and answered ISO 286 fit classes are preserved; writer verification checks the class against the answered limits. The oracle comparison can expand class limits only on its old intent face set, so the newly keyed full support reads as a class without numeric limits. Only these exact measured roots are covered; deferred owners remain unchanged.
